A.summary:
This change adds a new binary, benchmark_review, that scores sashiko's
reviews against a ground-truth file, benchmark.json. For each entry it
looks up the patch and its latest review in the database, then asks Gemini
whether any recorded finding or the review summary describes the known
problem. It also makes Gemini 429 handling honor the Retry-After header and
raises review concurrency in Settings.toml. A design document is added, and
several files get rustfmt-style reformatting with no behavior change.

Before:
  There was no way to score reviews against benchmark.json. On a 429,
  Gemini retries waited for the time parsed from the error body, or 30
  seconds if none was found. Settings.toml had review concurrency = 1.

After:
  Running "cargo run --bin benchmark_review" reads benchmark.json, queries
  the patches, reviews and findings tables, and makes one Gemini judge
  call per entry using the model from settings. It writes
  benchmark_results.json with one record per entry: commit,
  problem_description, found, status, explanation and findings_count. It
  logs totals for Detected, Partially Detected, Missed, Not Reviewed/Found
  and Skipped. The review concurrency setting also sets how many judge
  calls run in parallel.

  On a 429, the wait now uses the Retry-After header if it parses as a
  number of seconds, then the value from the error body, then 30 seconds.

  Settings.toml now has review concurrency = 24, so the main review
  pipeline also runs up to 24 reviews at once instead of 1.
A.inline_review:
- [HIGH] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry, main), the judge
  verdict is the first line of free-form model text with only [, ] and **
  stripped. It is never checked against DETECTED, PARTIALLY_DETECTED or
  MISSED. Replies like "DETECTED: finding 2...", "Detected", a leading
  non-text part ("Unknown"), or a Gemini failure ("ERROR", including an
  empty LLM_API_KEY) become arbitrary status strings and read as misses.
  The aggregation in main ends in "_ => {}", so these entries appear in no
  counter, the buckets do not sum to Total Entries, nothing warns, and the
  exit code is 0. The accuracy figure is plausible but false, and no test
  in the diff covers the parsing. Parse into a closed enum, add a counted
  error/unparsed status, exit non-zero when any exist, and unit-test a pure
  parse function with captured replies.

- [HIGH] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), infrastructure
  failures are recorded as benchmark outcomes. The reviews query uses
  ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 with no status filter, so a newer failed,
  FailedToApply or pending review with no findings is judged against
  "(No structured findings recorded in DB)" and scored MISSED. The reviews
  query maps Err(_) to None with no log, which reports NOT_REVIEWED. The
  findings query uses "if let Ok" and "while let Ok(Some(row))", so a query
  or row error becomes zero or truncated findings, then MISSED. The
  row.get(..).unwrap_or_default() calls turn decode errors into id 0 or
  empty text. main merges NOT_FOUND_IN_DB and NOT_REVIEWED, hiding DB
  errors as never-ingested patches. Filter on a completed review status,
  log or propagate every DB error, and report a distinct not-evaluable
  status. No test covers these paths.

- [MEDIUM] In Settings.toml ([review] concurrency), the shared key was
  raised from 1 to 24 to serve the new benchmark, but Reviewer::new in
  src/reviewer.rs sizes its Semaphore from the same value. The live
  reviewer service now runs 24 simultaneous reviews, each with its own git
  worktree of third_party/linux and its own Gemini tool-calling session,
  multiplying disk, CPU and API quota load and the chance of 429 storms.
  The commit gives no rationale. The benchmark also builds its own
  GeminiClient, bypassing the shared QuotaManager. Give the benchmark its
  own setting or CLI flag. A value of 0 makes buffer_unordered(0) poll
  nothing, writing an empty result file and exiting 0.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (main), arguments are never read.
  Running with --help or a mistyped flag opens the live DB, spends Gemini
  quota on the full run, and then File::create truncates the existing
  benchmark_results.json with no backup. Paths are hard-coded to the
  working directory and there is no dry-run or limit option.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (main), results are held in
  memory until every LLM call finishes, then streamed into a freshly
  truncated benchmark_results.json via serde_json::to_writer_pretty. A
  crash, panic or Ctrl-C loses the whole run, and a failure mid-write
  leaves invalid JSON with the previous good results already gone. Write a
  temp file and rename it. buffer_unordered also makes output order
  non-deterministic, so runs are hard to diff.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/gemini.rs (GeminiClient::post_request), the new
  Retry-After handling parses the header with parse::<f64>() and uses it
  unvalidated. Rust accepts NaN, inf, negative and exponent values.
  Duration::from_secs_f64(retry_seconds + 1.0) panics on NaN, infinity,
  values below -1 and overflow. A large finite value such as 1e9 makes
  GenAiClient::generate_content sleep with no upper bound. In
  benchmark_review a panic unwinds main and loses all results, since the
  output file is written only after collect(). The old body regex could not
  match these inputs, so this class is new. Triggering needs an unusual
  upstream or intercepting proxy value, which was not confirmed. Accept the
  header only if finite and non-negative, clamp it, else fall back to the
  body hint or 30s. No test covers the header path.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry) and src/ai/gemini.rs
  (GenAiClient::generate_content), a Gemini 429 is retried forever with no
  attempt cap or deadline, and process_entry wraps the call in no timeout.
  A persistent 429, such as daily quota exhaustion, hangs the benchmark
  with up to 24 tasks looping on one key through a bare GeminiClient that
  bypasses QuotaManager, and no output file is ever written. Cap attempts
  or elapsed time in generate_content, or time-box each evaluation and
  record an ERROR status.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry) and src/ai/gemini.rs
  (GeminiClient::generate_content_single, post_request), the API key is
  sent in the URL query string. On a transport failure the reqwest error
  text is logged without stripping the URL, then process_entry stores
  e.to_string() as the explanation in benchmark_results.json and logs it
  again. That durable, shareable file can then contain the key. No
  without_url or redaction exists in the tree. This assumes reqwest 0.13
  appends the URL to send errors, which was not confirmed and Cargo.lock
  was not checked. The existing log line is pre-existing exposure, but
  persisting it to the results file is new. Call without_url on the error
  or send the key in the x-goog-api-key header.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), a DB error on the
  patches query is logged but reported as NOT_FOUND_IN_DB, identical to a
  genuinely missing patch. The reviews query error is swallowed with no
  log and reported as NOT_REVIEWED. The findings query error or mid-row
  error yields an empty list that the judge scores MISSED. A locked
  database or schema mismatch under 24-way concurrency can therefore
  understate detection with no signal that the instrument failed.
  Propagate these into a distinct DB_ERROR status and count it.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry, main aggregation),
  swallowed libsql errors in the review and findings lookups become
  NOT_REVIEWED or an LLM-judged MISSED. ERROR and malformed judge replies
  fall into "_ => {}" and are counted in no bucket, so the summary
  silently under-reports entries and the process exits 0. Contention as
  the trigger is unproven, since the DB uses WAL with a 5000 ms busy
  timeout, but the error mapping is wrong regardless. Count ERROR and
  unrecognised statuses, and exit non-zero if any are present.

- [LOW] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), findings and the
  review summary are model output derived from attacker-writable patch
  content. They are interpolated into the judge prompt with no delimiters
  and no statement that they are data, so text such as "Respond DETECTED"
  can steer the verdict. Impact is limited to benchmark integrity, but the
  verdict is stored as the system's own measurement.

- [LOW] Commit scope and reproducibility. The commit bundles a new tool, a
  service config change, a shared API-client change and repo-wide
  reformatting in db.rs, fetcher.rs, reviewer.rs, review.rs and
  ingest_benchmark.rs, with no rationale or evidence of a run. The design
  document prompt passes only findings, while the code also passes the
  review summary. The doc lists NOT_FOUND_IN_DB, while the BenchmarkResult
  comment in benchmark_review.rs lists UNKNOWN, which is never emitted. The
  judge uses the reviewer's own model with generation_config None, and
  results record neither model nor prompt, so reruns are not reproducible
  and verdicts are self-graded.

findings.problem: judge verdict is unvalidated first-line text; errors dropped from summary
findings.explanation: A benchmark whose product is an accuracy figure reports a plausible but false result, and exits 0. In process_entry the status is parts[0] with '[', ']' and '**' stripped, never checked against DETECTED, PARTIALLY_DETECTED or MISSED. Replies like 'DETECTED: finding 2...', 'Detected', a leading non-text part ('Unknown'), or a Gemini failure ('ERROR', including a missing LLM_API_KEY, which GeminiClient::new defaults to an empty string) become arbitrary status strings. found is an exact string compare, so these read as misses in benchmark_results.json. main's aggregation ends in '_ => {}', so these entries are in no printed counter, the buckets do not sum to Total Entries, nothing warns, and the exit code is 0. The diff adds no test of the parsing, so none would fail. The fix is to parse into a closed enum, add an explicit error/unparsed status, count it, and exit non-zero when any exist. Extract a pure parse function and test it with captured replies.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Free-form model text becomes the recorded status; Err becomes 'ERROR'.
Unrecognised statuses and ERROR vanish from the summary.

findings.problem: DB errors and failed reviews are scored as MISSED or NOT_REVIEWED
findings.explanation: Infrastructure failures are recorded as benchmark outcomes, which deflates the measured detection rate with no signal. The reviews query takes 'ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1' with no status filter, so a newer failed, FailedToApply or pending review (statuses visible in db.rs tests) with no findings is sent to the judge as '(No structured findings recorded in DB)' and scored MISSED. The review query's 'Err(_) => None' reports NOT_REVIEWED with no log. 'if let Ok(mut rows) = findings_result' and 'while let Ok(Some(row))' turn a query or row error into zero or truncated findings, then MISSED. row.get(..).unwrap_or_default() turns decode errors into patch/review id 0 or empty text. The summary also merges NOT_FOUND_IN_DB and NOT_REVIEWED, so DB errors look like never-ingested patches. The diff has no test for any of these paths. The fix is to filter on a completed status, propagate or log every DB error, and report a distinct not-evaluable status.

findings.problem: shared review.concurrency raised 1 to 24 for the live service
findings.explanation: The reviewer service reads the same key as the benchmark (Reviewer::new, src/reviewer.rs:85/122 sizes its Semaphore from it), so the committed default makes the live reviewer run 24 simultaneous reviews, each with its own git worktree of third_party/linux and its own Gemini tool-calling session. That is 24x the disk, CPU and API-quota load, and it is much more likely to hit 429 retry storms. The benchmark also builds its own GeminiClient and so bypasses the shared QuotaManager the daemon uses, so 24 callers hit one key uncoordinated. It is a behaviour change to a running service, justified only by a benchmark tool, and the commit gives no rationale. The benchmark should get its own setting or CLI flag. Also, buffer_unordered(0) polls nothing, so a zero value would write an empty result file and exit 0.

findings.problem: --help or any flag runs the full benchmark and truncates results
findings.explanation: main() never reads arguments. 'cargo run --bin benchmark_review -- --help' opens the live DB, fires the concurrent Gemini calls (spending quota), and then File::create truncates the previous benchmark_results.json with no backup. A mistyped flag costs a full run and destroys earlier results. Paths are hard-coded to the CWD and there is no dry-run or limit option. Medium because it is an operator-invoked command with recoverable cost.

The repo rule is to write a temp file and rename. buffer_unordered also makes output order non-deterministic, which makes runs hard to diff.

findings.problem: Retry-After f64 header can panic Duration::from_secs_f64 on 429
findings.explanation: A panic in the 429 handler aborts the calling task, and a huge finite value stalls it. In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs the process_entry futures run under buffer_unordered inside main, so a panic unwinds main and every result is lost, because benchmark_results.json is written only after collect(). Reachability: any 429 from the Gemini endpoint whose Retry-After header is numeric but unusual. Rust f64 parse accepts NaN, inf, infinity, -5 and 1e300. Verified at 81f64ea: line 311 only does parse::<f64>().ok(), line 314 prefers the header over the body hint, and line 327 calls Duration::from_secs_f64(retry_seconds + 1.0) with no is_finite check, no clamp and no lower bound. from_secs_f64 panics on NaN, infinity, a negative result (header below -1) and overflow of Duration. A large finite value such as 1e9 does not panic but makes the loop in GenAiClient::generate_content run sleep(*sleep_duration) with no upper bound and then retry, so the task stalls for years. Before this commit the value came only from the body regex Please retry in ([0-9.]+)s, which cannot match a sign, NaN, inf or an exponent, so this input class is new and not preexisting. The dismissal argument holds only for HTTP-date headers, which fail the f64 parse and fall back to the regex or 30s. The request goes straight to generativelanguage.googleapis.com, so triggering this needs an upstream fault or a TLS-intercepting proxy, and I could not confirm that the real producer ever emits such values. That unverified assumption about the producer caps this at Medium. A fix is to accept the header only when it is finite and non-negative, clamp it to a sane maximum, and otherwise fall back to the body hint or 30s. No test in the diff covers the header path.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Accepts NaN, infinity, negative and arbitrarily large values from the response header with no validation.

findings.problem: benchmark_review retries Gemini 429 forever with no timeout
findings.explanation: Consequence: a persistent 429 (for example a daily quota exhaustion) makes src/bin/benchmark_review.rs hang indefinitely, and benchmark_results.json is only written after every entry completes, so the run produces no output at all. Reachability: every run of `cargo run --bin benchmark_review` builds a bare GeminiClient (benchmark_review.rs:64) and calls client.generate_content(req) (benchmark_review.rs:283). GenAiClient::generate_content for GeminiClient (src/ai/gemini.rs:346) is `loop { match self.generate_content_single(&request).await { Ok(resp) => return Ok(resp), Err(e) => { if let Some(GeminiError::QuotaExceeded(..)) ... { sleep(*sleep_duration).await; continue; } return Err(e); } } }`. It has no attempt counter and no deadline. This commit makes each retry sleep the Retry-After value, or the body hint, or 30s, plus 1s, and a Retry-After of 0 gives a 1s sleep. Nothing in the benchmark path wraps the call in tokio::time::timeout. buffer_unordered(settings.review.concurrency) is now 24 because Settings.toml changed concurrency from 1 to 24, so up to 24 tasks can sit in this loop against the one LLM_API_KEY. The benchmark also bypasses QuotaManager (src/ai/proxy.rs), so nothing coordinates the 24 retriers. The error is a 429, so each retry is rejected rather than billed; the cost is a stalled run and sustained request pressure on a quota-exhausted key, not lost money. The bound that exists elsewhere (see dismissed concern) does not cover this binary. Side effect: the same Settings.toml value raises production review concurrency to 24, which multiplies 429 pressure on the shared key. That is a config change and not itself a code defect. Capped at Medium because it is a developer tool with no money, credential or live-store effect. Fix: cap attempts or total elapsed time in generate_content, or wrap each process_entry evaluation in a timeout and record an ERROR status.

findings.problem: API key in URL leaks via reqwest error into benchmark_results.json
findings.type: Possible API key leak via reqwest error text
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: any transport failure (DNS, TLS, connect, timeout) in benchmark_review writes the Gemini API key in plaintext to benchmark_results.json and to the log. The file is a durable, shareable artifact whose purpose is to be inspected and passed around, and a leaked key cannot be un-leaked. Trigger path: process_entry calls client.generate_content(req), which calls generate_content_single, which builds the URL with format!("...:generateContent?key={}", self.model, self.api_key) and passes it to post_request. post_request runs self.client.post(url).json(body).send().await and propagates failure with `let res = res?;`, after logging it with `tracing::error!("Gemini request failed (transport): {}", e)`. generate_content in the GenAiClient impl returns non-quota errors unchanged (`return Err(e)`). process_entry then does `("ERROR".to_string(), e.to_string())` and stores it as `explanation`, and also logs it via error! and info!. Evidence checked: git_grep for without_url, redact and strip_url across the tree found nothing, so no stripping happens anywhere on this path. Cargo.toml pins reqwest = 0.13.1. I could not check Cargo.lock (git_grep and git_find_files returned no match at this revision), so the exact locked version is unverified. Assumption: reqwest's Error Display for send errors appends the request URL, in the form 'error sending request for url (<url>)'. That has been reqwest's behaviour since 0.11/0.12 and I expect it in 0.13, but I did not confirm it against the 0.13 source. If the URL is present, the key is in it, because it is passed as a query parameter. Confirm by forcing a connect failure (for example a bad proxy) and inspecting the explanation field. Because this rests on that unverified assumption, severity is capped at Medium. Pre-existing part: the log line at gemini.rs post_request already exposes the key in logs, and create_cached_content, list_cached_contents and delete_cached_content propagate raw `?` errors with the same URL form. This commit's new contribution is persisting the text in benchmark_results.json and logging it again, so the finding is marked not pre-existing. Fix: call e.without_url() on the reqwest error in post_request (and the cache methods) before logging or returning, or send the key in the x-goog-api-key header instead of the URL.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The raw error text is stored as explanation, written to benchmark_results.json, and logged.
The API key is embedded in the URL query string, so any error that prints the URL carries it.
The transport error is logged and propagated without without_url(), and no stripping exists anywhere in the tree.

findings.problem: DB errors in benchmark_review lookups scored as MISSED or NOT_FOUND
findings.type: Join key between benchmark.json and patches.message_id
findings.explanation: Consequence: a transient DB error (locked database, schema mismatch) during the patches, reviews or findings query is recorded as a benchmark outcome, so the summary can understate detection with no signal that the instrument failed. Reachability: every run of cargo run --bin benchmark_review, with 24 concurrent entries from Settings.toml against one libsql connection, so contention errors are plausible. The join key itself is sound (see dismissal), but the lookups around it fail silently. In process_entry, the patches query Err arm logs and sets patch_id to None, which becomes status NOT_FOUND_IN_DB with the explanation 'Patch not found in database.' The reviews query uses Err(_) => None, with no log at all, which becomes NOT_REVIEWED. The findings query uses if let Ok(mut rows) with no else arm, and a row-iteration error ends the loop through while let Ok(Some(..)). Either way findings_count stays 0, the prompt receives '(No structured findings recorded in DB)', and Gemini is asked to judge against an empty list, giving MISSED. That is a false negative counted as a real miss. Row decoding adds to this: row.get::<i64>(0).unwrap_or_default() turns a decode failure into patch_id 0, and the message and severity columns use unwrap_or_default. Gemini failures are labelled ERROR, which matches no counter in the summary, so those entries vanish from the printed totals. Nothing is fabricated about another program, and the severity is capped at Medium because the failure needs a DB error to trigger. A fix would propagate the errors into a distinct status such as ERROR or DB_ERROR and count it in the summary.

findings.problem: swallowed DB errors in benchmark_review scored as MISSED
findings.type: Shared libsql connection contention at 24-wide concurrency
findings.explanation: Consequence: any libsql error during the review or findings lookup in src/bin/benchmark_review.rs process_entry is turned into a plausible benchmark verdict (NOT_REVIEWED, or MISSED via the LLM judge) instead of a refused or errored cell. The Detected/Missed figures are the output of this instrument and are read by people deciding about review quality, so they are silently skewed. Reachability: runs for every benchmark entry via buffer_unordered(settings.review.concurrency), and this commit raises concurrency from 1 to 24 in Settings.toml. All tasks share one Database.conn, and the benchmark process runs next to a sashiko server that writes to the same file. Verified code: Database::new sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 on the connection. In WAL mode plain readers normally do not get SQLITE_BUSY from a concurrent writer, so I could not prove that 24-way contention produces BUSY on these SELECTs. The candidate's contention premise is therefore unproven, and this finding is capped at Medium. The real defect on the same path does not depend on contention: (1) the review query maps Err(_) => None with no log at all, which becomes NOT_REVIEWED. (2) The patch query logs the error but maps it to None, which becomes NOT_FOUND_IN_DB, the same status as a patch that really is absent. (3) The findings query uses if let Ok(mut rows) and while let Ok(Some(row)), so a query error or a mid-iteration error leaves findings_count at 0 or truncates the list. The prompt then says '(No structured findings recorded in DB)' and the judge returns MISSED, which counts as a real miss of the reviewer. row.get(...).unwrap_or_default() similarly turns a decode error into an empty message or severity 0. (4) When Gemini fails, status is 'ERROR', found is false, and the aggregation match has a '_ => {}' arm, so ERROR (and any judge reply whose first line is not exactly a status word, for example 'DETECTED: ...' on one line) is counted in no bucket. The printed counts then do not sum to Total Entries and nothing flags it. The process exits 0 in all cases. Git worktree part of the question: benchmark_review.rs never creates worktrees (it only uses the DB and Gemini). The concurrency=24 setting does apply to Reviewer (Semaphore::new(concurrency)). In src/git_ops.rs, GitWorktree::new runs 'git worktree add --detach' with no lock; only ensure_remote takes the per-remote and global config AsyncMutex locks. I did not prove that parallel worktree adds fail, so I report no separate finding for it. What would confirm contention failures: run the benchmark at 24 against a DB with an active server writer and count error! lines. Fix: propagate DB errors into a distinct DB_ERROR status, count ERROR and unrecognised statuses in the summary, and exit non-zero if any are present.

For a single commit, it overwrites message_id with commit_or_range, which is the submitted string. ingest_benchmark sends sha: entry.commit.clone(), and benchmark_review queries message_id = entry.commit from the same benchmark.json field. Both programs use the same string, so the key matches even for an abbreviated SHA. Uniqueness: Database::create_patch uses INSERT INTO patches ... ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO UPDATE SET patchset_id/part_index/diff. SQLite rejects an upsert target without a matching unique index, so message_id must be unique in the schema. I did not read the CREATE TABLE itself, because the UNIQUE grep in db.rs returned nothing, so the constraint is inferred from the upsert and the schema is not directly shown. Re-running ingest_benchmark therefore updates the one row and cannot create several rows for one sha, so the lack of ORDER BY cannot return an arbitrary row. The review lookup is keyed by patch_id with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1, so it is deterministic. Remaining risk: ingest_benchmark has no idempotency of its own, but the upsert absorbs that. B.summary:
This commit adds a standalone tool, benchmark_review, that scores
Sashiko's review output against a ground-truth corpus (benchmark.json).
For each entry it looks up the stored patch, its latest review and its
findings in the database. It then asks the configured Gemini model
whether any finding exactly describes the known problem, and writes the
verdicts to benchmark_results.json.

The commit also makes Gemini 429 handling honor the Retry-After header,
raises the shipped review concurrency in Settings.toml, adds a design
document, and includes some rustfmt-style reformatting of unrelated
files.

User-visible effects: a new binary, a changed default setting, and
changed rate-limit retry behavior.

Before:
  No tool existed to measure detection rate against benchmark.json.
  Settings.toml: concurrency = 1
  On a 429 response, the retry delay came only from the error body
  text, falling back to 30 seconds.

After:
  $ cargo run --bin benchmark_review
  Progress: 10/N ...
  Detected (Exact): N
  Partially Detected: N
  Missed: N
  Not Reviewed/Found: N
  Skipped (No Description): N
  Detailed results written to benchmark_results.json
  Settings.toml: concurrency = 24
  On a 429 response, the retry delay is taken from the Retry-After
  header if present, then from the error body, then 30 seconds.
B.inline_review:
- [HIGH] In src/ai/gemini.rs (GeminiClient::post_request), the reqwest
  transport error is logged with Display, which includes the request URL
  and therefore the ?key= API key value. The same error is propagated
  unredacted. The new process_entry in src/bin/benchmark_review.rs logs it
  and also stores e.to_string() in the explanation field of
  benchmark_results.json, so the key can be written to disk. Strip the URL
  from the error, pass the key in a header, or redact before logging.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry and the main
  aggregation loop), the judge verdict is taken verbatim from the first
  line of the reply with no check against DETECTED, PARTIALLY_DETECTED or
  MISSED. A reply such as "DETECTED: finding 2" or an ERROR/Unknown
  fallback yields found=false and matches no counter (the match ends in
  _ => {}). The printed counts then do not sum to Total Entries and
  nothing warns, so detection accuracy can be silently understated. No
  tests cover the verdict parsing.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), database errors
  are turned into false results. A failed review query maps to
  NOT_REVIEWED without logging, a failed findings query or row error
  yields zero findings and a false MISSED, and a decode failure on the
  patch id silently becomes 0 via unwrap_or_default. With 24 concurrent
  tasks, SQLITE_BUSY makes this plausible, and the benchmark numbers are
  skewed without any signal.

- [MEDIUM] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), the review
  lookup selects the latest review for the patch with no status filter.
  If the newest attempt is Failed, FailedToApply, Cancelled or still in
  progress, it has no findings and the judge reports MISSED even when an
  earlier successful review detected the bug.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/gemini.rs (GeminiClient::post_request), the new
  Retry-After header value is parsed as f64 with no validation and passed
  to Duration::from_secs_f64, which panics on negative, NaN, infinite or
  overflowing input. The old body-regex path could not produce such
  values. A very large finite value instead makes the retry loop in
  GenAiClient::generate_content sleep for that long with no cap. No test
  covers header precedence or edge values.

- [MEDIUM] Settings.toml raises review.concurrency from 1 to 24 with no
  rationale or evidence. Each permit in Reviewer::new holds a linux
  worktree and a worker subprocess, all writing through a database with
  only a 5 second busy_timeout. src/bin/benchmark_review.rs main reuses
  this daemon setting for its own parallelism instead of a tool-specific
  option, and does not reject a value of 0, which would hang silently.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::begin_transaction) and src/main.rs (DB
  worker batching loop), the ingest transaction is a raw BEGIN IMMEDIATE
  on the connection shared by all tasks and is held across awaits.
  Statements from reviewer and API tasks can run inside the batch and be
  committed or lost with it, and a failed COMMIT that is only logged
  leaves the transaction open so later batches fail. Raising concurrency
  to 24 in this commit makes this exposure more likely.

- [MEDIUM] In src/reviewer.rs (patch review loop and run_review_tool),
  review status transitions (Applying, InReview) and terminal
  complete_review writes are discarded with let _ = and nothing is
  logged, and Ok(PatchResult::Success) is returned regardless. If a write
  fails with SQLITE_BUSY, a review can stay in a non-terminal status with
  no findings and no error until the next restart. The 24-way concurrency
  default in this commit makes such contention more realistic.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/gemini.rs (GenAiClient::generate_content for
  GeminiClient and GeminiClient::new), the 429 retry loop has no attempt
  cap or deadline, and the client is built with Client::new() which sets
  no request or connect timeout. The new src/bin/benchmark_review.rs
  calls this path from up to 24 tasks with no shared QuotaManager, so a
  persistent 429 or a hung connection stalls the run indefinitely and
  each task retries independently.

- [LOW] The commit bundles a new benchmark binary and design document, a
  Gemini Retry-After behavior change, a Settings.toml concurrency change
  (1 to 24) and formatting-only edits in src/db.rs, src/fetcher.rs,
  src/reviewer.rs, src/bin/review.rs and src/bin/ingest_benchmark.rs. The
  commit message does not mention the formatting churn or justify the
  concurrency value, which makes bisecting and partial revert harder.

- [LOW] In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs (process_entry), the query on
  reviews filtered by patch_id has no supporting index, since src/schema.sql
  defines none on reviews(patch_id). Each benchmark entry scans the table
  at concurrency 24. Impact is limited to slower runs of an offline tool;
  confirm no runtime try_create_index call already covers it.

findings.problem: benchmark_review drops unrecognized judge verdicts from summary
findings.explanation: In src/bin/benchmark_review.rs, process_entry takes the first line of the Gemini reply, strips '[', ']' and '**', and stores it as the status without checking it against DETECTED, PARTIALLY_DETECTED or MISSED. A one-line reply such as 'DETECTED: finding 2...' or 'Status: MISSED' yields a garbage status and found=false, so a true detection is recorded as not found. The fallbacks 'Unknown' and 'ERROR' (Gemini failure) behave the same way. In main(), the aggregation match ends in '_ => {}', so these entries appear in no counter, the printed counts do not sum to Total Entries, and nothing warns about it. The tool exists to measure detection accuracy, so the numbers can be silently understated. The tool is a dev binary and does not affect the daemon, hence Medium. There are also no unit tests for the verdict parsing.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Unrecognized statuses (ERROR, Unknown, malformed) are excluded from the summary.
The verdict is taken verbatim from line 1 with no validation against the allowed set.

findings.problem: benchmark_review turns DB errors into false NOT_REVIEWED or MISSED
findings.explanation: In process_entry, the review query's 'Err(_) => None' reports a DB error (for example SQLITE_BUSY with 24 concurrent tasks) as NOT_REVIEWED, and the error is never logged. The findings query uses 'if let Ok(mut rows)' and 'while let Ok(Some(row))', so a query or iteration error leaves findings_count at 0. The prompt then says '(No structured findings recorded in DB)' and the judge answers MISSED, which counts an infrastructure failure against Sashiko's detection rate. 'row.get::<i64>(0).unwrap_or_default()' turns a decode failure into patch_id 0, so later queries run against the wrong id. Downstream impact: the benchmark accuracy numbers are silently skewed. The code is entirely visible in the new file.

findings.explanation: The review lookup is 'SELECT id, summary, result_description FROM reviews WHERE patch_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1' with no status predicate. findings.problem: Gemini API key leaks via reqwest transport error text in logs
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the secret is the primary-provider (Gemini) API key. It ends up in daemon logs and, with this patch, in an on-disk results file. It only leaks when a transport-level failure occurs (DNS, connect, TLS, timeout). Those are intermittent but realistic, and more likely at the 24-way concurrency this commit sets. The leak does not need an attacker, and the key stays valid until rotated, so this is High rather than Medium. It is not Critical because exposure is limited to operator-readable logs and output files, with no remote trigger. Proof: GeminiClient::generate_content_single and generate_content_with_cache_single build the URL as https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{}:generateContent?key={} using self.api_key (read from LLM_API_KEY). post_request sends it with self.client.post(url).json(body).send().await. On Err, it runs tracing::error!("Gemini request failed (transport): {}", e). Here e is a reqwest::Error, and its Display appends the request URL ("error sending request for url (...)"), query string included, so the key is printed. A grep of src/ai/ for without_url and redact_secret found no matches, so nothing strips the URL. The error is also propagated unredacted with `let res = res?;`. create_cached_content and list_cached_contents use the same ?key= URLs with `.send().await?` and also propagate the raw error. The patch makes this reachable in a new place: src/bin/benchmark_review.rs process_entry calls client.generate_content(req), then does error!("Error calling Gemini for commit {}: {}", entry.commit, e) and stores e.to_string() as the explanation field of BenchmarkResult. That field is serialized to benchmark_results.json, so the key can be written to a persistent file as well as the logs. The same commit also edits post_request (the 429 Retry-After handling) and raises review.concurrency to 24. Because the patch adds a caller that logs and persists this error, the finding is not marked preexisting. Fix: use e.without_url() when logging and propagating, or move the key into the x-goog-api-key header, or pass messages through crate::utils::redact_secret.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Logs reqwest::Error with Display, which includes the full request URL and therefore the ?key= query value; the error is then returned via res? with the URL still attached.
Places the API key in the URL query string, which is what ends up in the error text.

findings.problem: Gemini Retry-After header reaches from_secs_f64 unchecked
findings.type: Panic on untrusted input / missing test
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the failure needs a 429 response whose Retry-After header is negative, NaN, inf or very large. Real Gemini responses rarely carry such values, so this is a contained robustness defect, not a systematic break. Gemini is a primary provider, but I did not confirm every caller's handling, so this is capped at Medium. Proof from src/ai/gemini.rs at the target commit: in GeminiClient::post_request, the 429 branch parses the header with s.parse::<f64>().ok(). Rust's f64 parser accepts '-5', 'NaN', 'inf' and '1e30'. The patch gives the header priority over the body regex (`if let Some(secs) = retry_after_header { secs }`), and no is_finite, non-negative or maximum check follows. The value then goes straight into Duration::from_secs_f64(retry_seconds + 1.0) at line 327, which panics on negative, NaN, infinite or overflowing input. Before this patch only the body regex path existed, and its [0-9.]+ capture could not produce a negative, NaN or inf value. The header path is new and widens the set of values that reach the panic. A panic in this call is not mapped to a retry or a failed-review error: it unwinds the calling task. Separately, a large finite header value (for example 1e10) does not panic. It becomes a QuotaExceeded duration, and GeminiClient::generate_content (the loop around line 354) does sleep(*sleep_duration).await and continues with no cap and no attempt limit. That wedges the call for the full duration. benchmark_review (new in this patch) calls GeminiClient::generate_content directly through GenAiClient, so this loop is reached without any wrapper. I did not read the proxy.rs or reviewer.rs QuotaExceeded handlers (proxy.rs:108, reviewer.rs:1109 and 1177), so I could not confirm whether the daemon path clamps the value. Even if it does, the panic at line 327 happens before any caller sees the error. HTTP-date Retry-After values, which the HTTP spec allows, fail the f64 parse and silently fall back to the body regex or 30s. That is benign but unpinned. No test covers header precedence or the edge values.

locations.why_this_location_matters: New in this patch: accepts negative, NaN, inf and huge values from an external header with no validation.
Duration::from_secs_f64 panics on negative, NaN, inf or overflowing input, and nothing sanitizes retry_seconds first.
The retry loop sleeps for the server-supplied duration with no cap and no attempt limit, so a huge finite header value blocks the call for that long.

findings.problem: review.concurrency 1->24 in shipped Settings.toml, no rationale or guard
findings.explanation: Speculative, capped at Medium. Reasoning: the change multiplies per-daemon parallelism 24x. Reviewer::new (src/reviewer.rs:85,122) does Semaphore::new(settings.review.concurrency), and each permit holds a detached worktree of third_party/linux plus a worker subprocess and its LLM traffic. The Reviewer semaphore at this revision is exactly the setting, with no extra bound. Everything funnels through one shared libsql connection whose only contention protection is PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 (src/db.rs:304). Verified: (1) Settings.toml is the file parsed by test_production_settings_is_valid and read via Settings::new() from the CWD, but a grep of deployment/ and the Dockerfile found no SASHIKO__REVIEW__CONCURRENCY or Settings.toml reference, so I could not determine whether it is the deployed production config or a dev default. (2) benchmark_review (src/bin/benchmark_review.rs:69) reuses settings.review.concurrency for buffer_unordered, so the benchmark tool's parallelism is coupled to the daemon's default, and the commit raised the global default to suit a benchmark tool. A tool-specific knob would not change daemon behavior. (3) benchmark_review does not validate concurrency >= 1. With 0, buffer_unordered(0) never polls any entry and the stream hangs silently, while Reviewer's Semaphore::new(0) would never grant a permit. Settings requires the field, so this needs a deliberate 0 and is low likelihood. I could not verify: whether 24 concurrent worktree creations and DB writes actually hit SQLITE_BUSY beyond 5s, or whether quota/429 handling absorbs the extra LLM pressure. The commit message says only 'increase concurrency to 24' with no cost or contention evidence. This is not a trivial config tweak, because the value governs daemon disk, process and model spend. Not preexisting: the commit introduces the value.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Raises the daemon default 24x, with no rationale and no evidence that worktree, DB and quota paths cope.
Each permit maps to a linux worktree plus a worker subprocess, so the setting is a direct resource multiplier.
The only write-contention mitigation on the shared connection when 24 reviews persist results concurrently.
The benchmark tool reuses the daemon setting instead of its own knob, and nothing checks concurrency >= 1, so 0 hangs silently.

findings.problem: batch ingest txn runs on shared connection, absorbing concurrent writes
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the candidate's literal claim (two tasks calling begin_transaction concurrently) is wrong, but a related defect is real. At 81f64eaa, Database is just `pub struct Database { pub conn: libsql::Connection }` (src/db.rs:23-25). There is no tx_lock, tx_conn or DatabaseTransaction, and begin_immediate_transaction does not exist. begin_transaction (src/db.rs:1025-1028) runs a raw `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on self.conn, and commit_transaction (1030-1033) runs a raw `COMMIT`. A grep of src finds exactly one caller, the single DB-worker task in src/main.rs:424/445, so two concurrent BEGINs from this path cannot occur. However, that worker holds its transaction open across `.await`s while calling process_parsed_article (main.rs:431) on the same Arc<Database>. The Reviewer (main.rs:492, ctx.db = self.db.clone(), reviewer.rs:209/676), the API (main.rs:481) and the other workers share that same libsql connection, and libsql clones share one sqlite3 handle. Statements issued by those tasks while the batch is open therefore run inside the ingest transaction. Their writes are committed or lost together with the batch, and a failed COMMIT (main.rs:445 only logs it) leaves the transaction open, so the next BEGIN IMMEDIATE fails with 'cannot start a transaction within a transaction' and the loop skips every later batch. This commit raises review.concurrency from 1 to 24 in Settings.toml, so many more reviewer tasks now write through the shared connection while ingestion batches are open. That makes the exposure materially more likely, hence preexisting=false. Severity is capped at Medium: the impact is a localized state/ordering hazard that depends on timing and on libsql's shared-handle semantics (which I did not test), and reviewer writes would be lost only in the failed-commit case. This violates the patterns/concurrency.md invariant that transactions go through tx_lock/tx_conn.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Raw transaction on the connection shared by every task holding the Arc<Database>, with no serialization or RAII rollback.
Opens the transaction and holds it across many awaits while other tasks use the same connection; a failed commit at line 445 is only logged and leaves it open.
This commit raises concurrent reviewer DB activity on the shared connection by 24x, exposing the hazard.

findings.problem: review status and completion DB write errors are silently dropped
findings.explanation: Reasoning: this is a contained, per-review bookkeeping defect, not a daemon-wide failure. It is speculative on how likely contention is, because I could not show that the 5s busy_timeout is actually exceeded, so it is capped at Medium. The candidate's 'row stuck forever' premise is partly wrong. When update_review_status(Applying) or update_review_status(InReview) fails, the later complete_review call in the same flow normally overwrites the status, and the startup recovery query in src/db.rs resets rows in 'Applying' or 'In Review' to Pending after a restart. However, every one of these writes is discarded with 'let _ =' and nothing is logged. That includes the terminal complete_review calls in Database-backed review handling in src/reviewer.rs, for example the Reviewed, Failed and FailedToApply branches. They are followed by return Ok(PatchResult::Success) or ReviewFailed regardless of whether the write succeeded. Each review child process opens its own connection to the same SQLite file, and Database::new sets a fixed 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000'. This commit raises review.concurrency in Settings.toml from 1 to 24, so cross-process writer contention is now a real configuration. If a write fails with SQLITE_BUSY, the failure is invisible. A completed review can then stay at 'Applying' or 'In Review' with no findings, no logs and no error message until the next daemon restart. That is the 'silence looks like a clean patch' failure mode. It is not preexisting because the 24-way concurrency change exposes it. The fix is to log or propagate these errors, and to retry complete_review on busy errors.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The InReview transition result is discarded and ai_started is set to true anyway, so the transition is never retried. The same pattern appears at line 1136 for ai_request_with_cache.
The Applying transition error is swallowed with no log.

The terminal write is also discarded and Ok(PatchResult::Success) is returned, so a failed final write leaves the row in a non-terminal status. The same applies to the Failed and FailedToApply branches.
A fixed 5s busy wait is shared by every review child process and the daemon, and the concurrency default is now 24.

findings.problem: unbounded 429 retry and no HTTP timeout used by benchmark_review
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the impact is limited to the offline benchmark_review binary, a developer-run tool and not the daemon review path, so it is capped at Medium. It can stall or run up cost, but it does not corrupt data or send mail. The code shows three things. (1) GenAiClient::generate_content for GeminiClient in src/ai/gemini.rs is a bare loop. On GeminiError::QuotaExceeded it sleeps and continues, with no attempt cap and no total deadline. A persistent 429, such as an exhausted daily quota, therefore never returns an error. (2) GeminiClient::new builds its client with reqwest::Client::new(), which sets no request or connect timeout. One hung connection in post_request blocks that task, and its buffer_unordered slot, forever. (3) The patch adds this exposure. benchmark_review::process_entry calls client.generate_content(req) on a bare GeminiClient from up to settings.review.concurrency tasks, and this commit raises that value from 1 to 24 in Settings.toml. The tasks share no QuotaManager, unlike the production paths in src/reviewer.rs (lines ~1106 and ~1174) and src/ai/proxy.rs, which call generate_content_single and report_quota_error to the shared manager. Each of the 24 tasks therefore retries independently, which multiplies 429 pressure. The new Retry-After handling in post_request feeds the same loop. A secondary hazard is that the header value is parsed with parse::<f64>() and never validated. A negative, NaN or infinite value would reach Duration::from_secs_f64(retry_seconds + 1.0), which panics; the panic would be unwinding inside a buffer_unordered task and take down the whole benchmark run. Google is unlikely to send such values, so this is low likelihood. Unanswered question: I did not confirm whether the reviewer.rs:104 client reaches generate_content (the unbounded loop) in production or only generate_content_single. The Medium cap therefore rests on the benchmark_review path alone.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The retry loop has no attempt cap or deadline, so a persistent 429 never returns an error.
The client has no request or connect timeout, so a hung connection stalls the task indefinitely.

findings.problem: benchmark_review queries reviews by patch_id with no supporting index
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the missing index only turns a lookup into a table scan. The affected query runs once per benchmark entry in an offline, operator-run binary, not in the daemon's hot path, so the impact is slower benchmark runs and not data loss or a service failure. Verified: src/schema.sql defines 'reviews' (lines 96-113) with 'patch_id INTEGER' and a foreign key to patches(id), but the only CREATE INDEX statements next to it are idx_findings_review_id and idx_findings_severity on findings. There is no index on reviews(patch_id). A grep of src/ for idx_reviews and for 'reviews.*patch_id' index definitions found none, and the src/migrations grep returned no INDEX statements. SQLite does not create an index for a foreign key. The new query 'SELECT id, summary, result_description FROM reviews WHERE patch_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1' in src/bin/benchmark_review.rs:181 therefore scans reviews for each entry, run at concurrency 24. The same pattern is used by production paths in src/db.rs (count_successful_reviews at line 521 and the check at line 542, both filtering on patchset_id AND patch_id). dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: benchmark_review looks up patches via message_id = commit SHA, but the mapping from the benchmark Commit field to patches.message_id is unverified, so every entry could report NOT_FOUND_IN_DB.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: I traced the full ingestion path for benchmark patches. (1) ingest_benchmark submits Remote{sha, repo} to /api/submit. In src/api.rs, submit_patch turns it into FetchRequest{repo_url, commit_hash: sha}. (2) In src/fetcher.rs, extract_patch returns PatchSubmitted with message_id: String::new() and the comment 'Set by caller'. The caller then overwrites it: *message_id = sha.clone() for the range path (line 223) and *message_id = commit_or_range.clone() for the single-commit path (line 249). (3) In src/main.rs, the PatchSubmitted handler copies that message_id unchanged into both PatchsetMetadata.message_id and Patch.message_id. (4) The ingest worker calls worker_db.create_patch(patchset_id, &patch.message_id, ...) at src/main.rs:796-799. db.rs create_patch inserts that string into patches.message_id, and the ON CONFLICT(message_id) clause only updates patchset_id, part_index and diff, never message_id. I found no db.rs code that rewrites patches.message_id afterwards. The cover-letter and thread ids use the separate '<article_id>@sashiko.local' form and do not touch patches.message_id. So patches.message_id equals exactly the string that ingest_benchmark submitted as sha, which is the benchmark Commit value. The lookup in benchmark_review is therefore consistent for both the single-commit and range cases. The lack of a seeded-DB test is a test-coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect, and the design doc wording ('likely corresponds') does not change the verified behavior.

locations.why_this_location_matters: For ranges, each emitted patch gets message_id equal to the bare commit SHA.
For single commits, message_id equals the submitted SHA string.
The unmodified message_id is persisted into patches.message_id, which is the column benchmark_review queries.
